elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binding Customer (IBM)
elements.evidence: "IBM agrees that, for a period of twelve (12) months ... it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees"

elements.element: Fallback: restriction is mutual (binds both Customer and Vendor)
elements.evidence: Only "IBM agrees that ... it will not in any way solicit"; no reciprocal MSL obligation appears.

elements.element: Fallback: scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services
elements.evidence: "any Transferred Employees" — no limitation to personnel directly involved in the Services.

elements.element: Fallback: period runs from the end of the individual's involvement
elements.evidence: "twelve (12) months from the Effective Date of this Agreement"
"by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto"
"employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM"
Restriction is only on "solicit for employment"; hiring via the carve-outs is expressly permitted.

reasons: The edit changes only the duration; the clause remains a one-way restriction on the Customer (IBM), so the fallback's express mutuality is absent.
Scope is still "any Transferred Employees" rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, so the population restricted is broader than the fallback permits.
The 12-month period runs "from the Effective Date of this Agreement" rather than from the end of each individual's involvement, which is the fallback trigger.
Carve-outs for unsolicited contact and general advertising, and the absence of any no-hire, are satisfied as drafted.

The change is narrowly scoped (a single duration operator) and introduces no undefined terms or dangling mechanics, so minimality and intent preservation are satisfied; however the fallback bargain is incomplete on mutuality, scope, and the duration trigger.
